simple.meaning: נַעֲמָתִי (Naʻămâthîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a Naamathite , or inhabitant of Naamah.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נַעֲמָתִי (H5284) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 2:11, with occurrences in Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נַעֲמָתִי (H5284) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נַעֲמָתִי (H5284) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נַעֲמָתִי (Naʻămâthîy) / H5284 is traced through Job 2:11, Job 11:1, Job 20:1, Job 42:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a Naamathite , or inhabitant of Naamah
definitions.full: H5284. Naamathi נַעֲמָתִי adjective, of a people (from unused proper name); — הַנּ ׳צוֺפַר Job 2:11 ( ᵐ5 ὁ Μειναίων βασιλεύς ), 11:1 ; 20:1 ; 42:9 (all ᵐ5 ὁ Μειναῖος ); Hom Aufsätze 48 proposes מְעוּנִי .
definitions.rootNote: patrial from a place corresponding in name (but not identical) with 5279 ;

occurrences.englishText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.
